scenario.name: definition
scenario.context: A microcontroller is a small computer on a single chip. It contains a CPU, memory and input/output peripherals. It is commonly used in embedded systems.

title: Microcontroller Basics
bullets: A microcontroller is a small computer integrated onto a single chip
It includes a central processing unit (CPU), memory, and input/output peripherals
Commonly used in embedded systems for controlling electronic devices

scenario.name: comparison
scenario.context: A microcontroller combines the CPU, memory and peripherals on one chip. A microprocessor mainly contains the CPU and usually depends on external memory and peripherals.

title: Microcontroller vs Microprocessor: Core Differences
bullets: Microcontroller: Integrates CPU, memory, and peripherals on a single chip
Microprocessor: Contains only CPU and requires external memory/peripherals
Microcontrollers are self-contained systems for embedded applications
Microprocessors are used in general-purpose computing systems

scenario.name: process
scenario.context: First the sensor captures the physical signal. The ADC converts the analog signal into digital data. The CPU processes the digital data. Finally the system sends the result to the actuator.

title: Sensor Data Processing Workflow
bullets: Physical signal captured by sensor
Analog signal converted to digital data via ADC
CPU processes the digital data
System sends processed result to actuator

scenario.name: architecture
scenario.context: A microcontroller contains a CPU, RAM, program memory, input/output ports, timers and communication peripherals. These components work together inside the microcontroller.

title: Microcontroller Architecture Overview
bullets: A microcontroller integrates a CPU for processing instructions
RAM provides temporary storage for data during operation
Program memory stores the firmware or software code
Input/output ports enable interaction with external devices
Timers manage time-based operations and intervals
Communication peripherals facilitate data exchange with other systems

scenario.name: examples
scenario.context: Examples include Arduino Uno, ESP32, STM32, PIC and AVR microcontrollers.

title: Common Microcontroller Examples
bullets: Arduino Uno: Popular open-source platform for beginners
ESP32: Dual-core processor with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities
STM3: 32: High-performance microcontroller for industrial applications
PIC: Family of microcontrollers with simple architecture
AVR: Microcontrollers with 8-bit and 32-bit variants

scenario.context: Controller A operates at 16 MHz, controller B operates at 32 MHz, and controller C operates at 80 MHz.
